headline: Set-level reinforcement learning improves judged quality and diversity of scientific idea portfolios
summary: The Oct 15 arXiv preprint introduces a set-level reinforcement-learning objective that scores each idea by its judged quality and semantic distance from earlier ideas in the same generated set. The authors train Qwen3-8B and report a Creative Utility score of 0.64 for the no-thinking variant and 0.51 for the thinking variant on a 1,740-instance, contamination-free test set built from 2026 papers; the reported baselines are 0.38 for Claude Opus 4.8 and 0.28 for GPT-6 Astra. A four-expert pilot across 60 instances reports similar counts of promising ideas to Claude and slightly more unique ideas, while a coding-agent proof-of-concept on 15 instances reports comparable success@k. These are author-reported results using model-based evaluation; the author-linked code repository currently says code, data and models are forthcoming.
